records.title: NetStack: A Game Approach to Synthesizing Consistent Network Updates
records.support_location: PDF pp. 2-3: Sections II.C-D; pp. 5-6: Proposition 1, Corollary 1 and Section III.C; p. 7: Section IV; pp. 7-8: Section V.
records.cited_claim: NetStack minimizes concurrent update rounds safe under every within-round update order, for fixed initial/final routings and at most one update per router.
records.evidence_summary: Sections II.C-D define one initial-to-final update per changing node and safety for all subsets and permutations within a batch. Section IV assigns zero cost to batch membership and unit cost to advancing a round. The Stackelberg solution supplies a minimum-batch schedule when one exists. Sections III.C and V describe BDD-based symbolic planning and a timed synthesis evaluation.
records.correction_or_boundary: Minimum safe batches are established prior work. For binary one-change catalogs with the same configuration predicate, their batch objective coincides with the present phase objective; this equivalence is an inference from the two definitions. The source does not supply the present durable guard-handoff protocol. No source code or live router deployment was re-executed in this audit.
records.metadata_action: Added closest primary update-synthesis source; institutional author record verifies venue, year and DOI. Page range omitted because it was not independently verified from publisher metadata.

records.title: AllSynth: A BDD-based approach for network update synthesis
records.support_location: Printed pp. 4-5: Section 2.2, Definitions 5-7; pp. 10-12: Section 3.2, update-sequence encodings and Theorem 1; pp. 12-13: Section 4, Definitions 9-10.
records.cited_claim: AllSynth represents correct simple and repeated-router update sequences and optimizes the worst intermediate forwarding-path weight.
records.evidence_summary: Definition 7 distinguishes one initial-to-final update per node from general sequences allowing repeated node changes. Section 3.2 encodes all correct sequences of a specified length symbolically. Definition 10 minimizes the largest forwarding-path weight among intermediate configurations.
records.correction_or_boundary: The Section 4 objective is not a minimum concurrent-round objective. General repeated updates and symbolic complete solution sets are already studied. No performance comparison with RolloutFrontier is asserted.
records.metadata_action: Added relevant journal source using the publisher PDF from the author institution. Repository cover and publisher metadata verify title, volume 230, article 102992 and DOI.
records.category: symbolic update synthesis and cost optimization

records.title: Synthesizing Runtime Programmable Switch Updates
records.support_location: PDF p. 5: Section 3 atomic change annotations; pp. 6-8: Section 4.1 sequence sketches; pp. 9-10: Sections 4.3-4.4 iterative deepening and finite-search guarantees.
records.cited_claim: FlexPlan synthesizes safe program snapshots by increasing sequence length under switch-memory constraints.
records.evidence_summary: Section 4.1 encodes initial and final programs, forward progress, safe snapshots and per-transition resource spikes. Section 4.3 increases candidate sequence length from one to the finite change-count bound. Section 4.4 explains completeness from finite candidate space and CEGIS. Section 3 supplies the atomic change-annotation premise.
records.correction_or_boundary: Target-directed multi-step synthesis is an established capability. An atomic program-snapshot transition is not automatically the same cost or safety unit as a phase retaining every intermediate physical version.
records.metadata_action: Upgraded source support from abstract-only classification to selected full-text passages.
records.category: network control, update, and venue calibration

records.title: Projection Methods for Finding the Greatest Element of the Intersection of Max-Closed Convex Sets
records.support_location: Section 2.2: Proposition 1, Equation (7), Lemma 4 and Theorem 2; Section 2.3: Proposition 2.
records.cited_claim: Decreasing projection finds greatest feasible points below an upper bound and is monotone for closed max-closed sets; the stated intersection-convergence theorems additionally assume convexity.
records.evidence_summary: Proposition 1 identifies a greatest feasible element below the given point for closed max-closed sets, including nonconvex sets. Proposition 2 establishes monotonicity on the domain where projection exists. Theorem 2 separately assumes max-closed closed convex sets for convergence of cyclic decreasing projections.
records.correction_or_boundary: Nonconvexity alone is not a novelty distinction. The present result requires contiguous physical prefixes, proves safety of their full interval product, and minimizes the number of such phases.
records.metadata_action: Refined source-specific attribution to avoid treating all greatest-element and monotonicity results as convex-only.

records.title: Interactive Checks for Coordination Avoidance
records.support_location: Author manuscript pp. 11-14: Sections 6.1-6.4, especially p. 14 Section 6.4 on programmer-supplied segmentation.
records.cited_claim: Lucy permits local execution inside a valid segment, coordinates across boundaries, and takes programmer-supplied segmentation as input.
records.evidence_summary: Section 6.1 defines invariant-confluent segments; Sections 6.1-6.2 allow local execution inside a segment and coordination at boundaries. Section 6.4 explicitly leaves segmentation construction to the programmer.
records.correction_or_boundary: Current specific claim remains supported. The work already provides repeated protected execution, so it should not be described as static-only.

records.title: The Homeostasis Protocol: Avoiding Transaction Coordination Through Program Analysis
records.support_location: Sections 3.3 and 4.2, PDF pp. 5-7: repeated rounds, local treaty synthesis and sampled future-execution MaxSAT optimization.
records.cited_claim: Homeostasis derives local treaties, repeats generation, disconnected execution and cleanup, and selects treaties using sampled future executions.
records.evidence_summary: Section 3.3 describes repeated protocol rounds. Section 4.2 synthesizes local predicates whose conjunction enforces the global treaty, and chooses configurations by a MaxSAT objective over sampled possible future executions.
records.correction_or_boundary: Already synthesizes treaties and repeats rounds. Compare the declared target/guard planning objective, not an asserted absence of synthesis or repeated coordination.

records.title: Optimal Consistent Network Updates in Polynomial Time
records.support_location: Author manuscript Section 3 pp. 5-7; Section 4.3 Lemma 2; Section 5 Algorithms 1/3 and Theorems 4-6 pp. 9-12. Publisher metadata verifies final pp. 114-128.
records.cited_claim: Cerny et al. give a polynomial greedy minimum-round algorithm for single-flow per-packet consistency, with at most one change per switch and safety checked on unions of configurations between waits.
records.evidence_summary: The model updates each changing node once from its initial to final forwarding rules. Consistency requires every maximal ingress path to occur in the initial or final configuration. A round is safe only if the union of its configurations satisfies this condition. Lemma 2 and the careful-sequence reduction support the greedy algorithm; Theorems 4-6 establish its optimality and correctness.
records.correction_or_boundary: Greedy minimum-round planning in a structured update model is established prior work. The persistent updatability property is proved for careful sequences. Per-packet union safety is not merely independent snapshot safety; no equivalence or inclusion with the present max-closed class is claimed. The extended proof manuscript and implementation were not independently checked.
records.metadata_action: Added closest structured minimum-round source. Publisher chapter metadata verifies authors, venue, LNCS volume 9888, pp. 114-128, year and DOI.
